title: Brandl et al. 2020 — Motor Imagery Under Distraction: An Open Access BCI Dataset
description: An open-access EEG dataset of a two-class motor imagery brain-computer interface experiment conducted under distraction. Sixteen healthy participants imagined left- or right-hand movements while exposed to six conditions: no distraction, eyes closed, news listening, number search, flickering video, and vibro-tactile stimulation. Each participant completed one calibration run and six feedback runs (504 trials in total), recorded with 63 EEG channels at 1000 Hz.
methods_description: Each participant completed a single session of 7 runs with 72 trials per run. Run 1 was a calibration run without feedback or distraction. Runs 2-7 gave auditory feedback, each under one distraction condition. Auditory cues ('links'/'rechts') indicated left- or right-hand motor imagery. Trials lasted 4.5 s with a 2.5 s inter-trial interval. EEG was recorded with two BrainAmp amplifiers and EasyCap Ag/AgCl wet electrodes (63 channels, nose reference, 1000 Hz). Online classification used CSP with LDA in the BBCI Toolbox.
